assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Continents or Pangaea, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Seondeok has a single persona and that is the one planned here. The shape is Front-Load because the Seowon must stand on a hill, loses Science to every district placed beside it, and can never be moved, so the hills chosen and the tiles left empty around them by turn 20 set the Science ceiling for the whole game. The kit itself is flat: it pays the same on turn 40 as on turn 200.

verdict.one_line: Settle on hills, pin a Seowon two tiles out of every city with nothing ever built beside it and Mines and Farms all around it, pour every Governor title into promotions for Hwarang, and spend the early Science lead on a space race finished around turn 250, before rivals' adjacency catches up.
verdict.why: Korea cannot build a Campus at all; its Science district is the Seowon, which must sit on Hills and has a flat +4 Science that loses a point for every district beside it. Science is therefore a count of isolated Seowon hills on the settle map, fixed before turn 20, not a function of mountains, reefs or district clusters. Three Kingdoms adds a Science to every Mine around a Seowon and Hwarang adds three percent per Governor promotion, so Korea has the highest Science on most Emperor maps from the Classical era with almost no tuning. The same flatness is the limit: nothing lifts a Seowon above its base, and rivals with +5 and +6 Campuses close the gap once Research Labs arrive. Science is the victory because the lead is real and early, and it is cashed fast. Domination is the secondary because the Hwacha brings Field Cannon firepower at Machinery, and a tech lead that cannot win the space race can still win a war against the civ that is beating you to it, provided your army tech matches theirs.

must_have: A hill on or beside the start tile, and at least one more hill in its second ring with three free neighbours for Mines and Farms.
Hills for at least four more Seowon sites within about twelve tiles of the capital, each with its own ring of six tiles that no other city needs.
prefer: Grassland hills, which feed the citizens who work the Mines around each Seowon.
Iron, Niter, Coal and later Aluminum on hills next to a Seowon hill, so the strategic Mine also earns the Three Kingdoms Science and counts for Taruga.
A Mountain touching at least one Seowon hill, for the Astronomy Eureka on that city's University; the Mountain costs the Seowon nothing.
A river past the far side of the capital for the Aqueduct and, later, Ruhr Valley beside an Industrial Zone.
Yosemite beside a Seowon ring: its Science on adjacent tiles stacks on the Mines there.
map_check.no_go: A flat start of floodplain, desert flats or open tundra with no hill within two moves and fewer than three hill sites in view. Korea has no Campus to fall back on: without hills there is no Science district at all, and the kit shrinks to Hwarang.
map_check.fallback: Move up to two tiles toward the nearest hills. If none appear, settle and say plainly that Korea is now a generic civ with Hwarang: Seowons on whatever hills exist, even in the first ring at +3, Pingala in the capital with every promotion, Commercial Hubs and Theater Squares for the yields the Seowons cannot provide, and the Hwacha at Machinery to take a neighbour's hill country for the Seowon sites the start lacked.

kit_levers.name: Hwarang
kit_levers.buys: Each promotion an established Governor has earned adds three percent Culture and three percent Science in the city that Governor is assigned to.
kit_levers.exploit: Titles go into depth, not breadth. Pingala sits in the capital and takes every promotion he has (Researcher, Connoisseur, Grants, Space Initiative, Curator), five promotions on top of his own Science and Culture bonus. A second Governor in the second-best Seowon city takes the next titles. No third Governor is appointed until Pingala has three promotions, and an established Governor is never moved except to save a city, because re-establishing costs turns of the bonus.

kit_levers.name: Three Kingdoms
kit_levers.buys: Mines adjacent to a Seowon gain +1 Science and Farms adjacent to a Seowon gain +1 Food.
kit_levers.exploit: The six tiles around each Seowon, called its ring in this plan, are the best tiles in the city: Mines on hills and resources, Farms on flats. The yield is on the tile, so it only counts while a citizen works it; the ring is worked before any other tile, and rings of different cities are drawn not to overlap because a tile is worked by one city at a time.

kit_levers.name: Seowon
kit_levers.buys: A Campus replacement at half the cost that must be built on Hills, with a flat +4 Science that drops by 1 for each adjacent district.
kit_levers.exploit: The first district in every city, placed on a pinned hill in the second ring, where it touches neither the City Center nor any later district. It still counts as a Campus for Libraries, Universities, Research Labs, Recorded History, Divine Spark, Natural Philosophy and Great Scientist points. Every other district goes on the far side of the city and gives up the adjacency the Seowon would have lent it.

kit_levers.name: Hwacha
kit_levers.buys: A Field Cannon replacement unlocked by Machinery in the Medieval era, with Field Cannon Ranged Strength centuries early, that cannot move and attack in the same turn.
kit_levers.exploit: Two Hwacha on a hill behind each border city's Walls hold any Medieval or Renaissance attack while every hammer stays on Seowons. If a neighbour's hill country sits within eight tiles, four Hwacha and two melee units take two of its cities around turn 110, and each captured city gets a Seowon pinned the turn it falls.

kit_levers.name: Cheomseongdae
kit_levers.buys: AI Seondeok values Science and dislikes civilizations that produce little of it.
kit_levers.exploit: Irrelevant to your own play. It is a reminder that the AI civs worth befriending are the scientific ones: a Research Alliance with the highest-Science neighbour is the Diplomatic Service Inspiration and, at level 2, the Chemistry Eureka.

turn_zero: Before the Settler moves: take the hill inventory. List every hill in the second and third rings of the start tile and, for each, count how many of its six neighbours are hills or flat land that could hold a Mine or a Farm and that no other district will ever need. One hill with three or more such neighbours: settle in place. None: move up to two tiles toward the nearest cluster of hills and count again. No hill within two moves is the no-go.

Before the Settler moves: settle on a hill if one is on or beside the start tile, but never on the hill you want for the Seowon. The Seowon goes in the second ring. In the first ring it touches the City Center and is +3 for the whole game; in the third ring half its ring of Mines lies outside the city's reach.

Before the Settler moves: pin the Seowon hill and its ring, the six tiles around it. They are Mines on hills and resources (+1 Science each) and Farms on flats (+1 Food each). No district of any kind is ever placed on a ring tile, the Aqueduct, Neighborhood, Government Plaza, Dam and Spaceport included. A wonder may go there; it does not reduce the Seowon, it only costs a Mine.

Before the Settler moves: pin the far side. The Commercial Hub, Theater Square, Industrial Zone and Aqueduct go on the opposite side of the City Center from the Seowon, touching each other and the center. They get nothing from the Seowon and it gets nothing from them; that is the price of the +4, and it is paid in every city.

Turns 1 to 3: research Mining, then Pottery, then Writing. The Scout heads for the nearest rival so first contact gives the Writing Eureka. The Seowon is the critical path; Astrology, Animal Husbandry and Bronze Working wait.
By turn 10: mark every hill the Scout has revealed that can be the Seowon hill of cities two to eight, each with its own ring that does not overlap the capital's ring or each other's.
front_load.ceiling: One Seowon per city at a flat +4 Science, +8 while Natural Philosophy and later Five-Year Plan double it, plus +1 Science on every worked Mine in its ring, multiplied by Hwarang in the two or three cities with heavily promoted Governors. With eight to ten Seowon cities that is the top Science on most Emperor maps from turn 40 to about turn 160. It cannot be raised: no Seowon gains from a neighbouring district, Mountain or Reef, so a rival with +5 or +6 Campuses closes the gap in the Industrial era once Research Labs multiply what each district makes. The ceiling is the number of isolated Seowon hills drawn by turn 20, and the plan spends the lead on a space race finished around turn 250 rather than a long game.

irreversibles.decision: Capital tile, which fixes the capital's Seowon hill and its ring; the Seowon must sit in the second ring of this tile.
Capital Seowon placed on its pinned hill. A placed district never moves, even unfinished, and every district later placed beside it costs a point of Science for the rest of the game.

The settle map: cities two to eight, each chosen for a second-ring Seowon hill with its own ring, drawn before the second Settler is queued. A city founded without one has no Science district, ever, because Korea cannot build a Campus.

The Governor plan. Promotions cannot be refunded and Hwarang pays per promotion, so every title after the second goes into promotions on Pingala in the capital and one other Governor, not into a third, fourth and fifth Governor.
The far side of every city. The first non-Seowon district placed fixes where that city's cluster grows; one placed against the ring takes a Mine and a point of Seowon Science in the same move.

front_load.settle_map_rule: Draw cities two to eight before the second Settler is queued, on sites about four tiles apart center to center. A site qualifies only if it has a hill in its second ring whose six neighbours hold at least three hills or flat tiles for Mines and Farms that are in no other city's ring and on no other city's far side. Mark, for every site, the city tile, the Seowon hill, its ring, and the far side for the Commercial Hub, Theater Square, Industrial Zone and Aqueduct. A site with good land and no qualifying hill is skipped, not settled: Korea cannot build a Campus, so that city never has a Science district. Cities seven and eight may be fifty turns away; they are drawn now so that cities three and four do not take their hills.

phases.name: Assess and commit
phases.objective: Take the hill inventory, settle so the capital's Seowon hill sits in the second ring, pin its ring and the far side, research Mining, Pottery and Writing, place the Seowon on its pin the turn Writing lands, and draw cities two to eight with their hills before the second Settler is queued. Every decision that caps this game is made in these twenty turns.

build_order.why: Meets the first civilization for the Writing Eureka and reveals the hills that cities two to eight will be drawn on.
The capital's defender while the Scout is away; the Archery Eureka on the first barbarian it finishes.
City two on its drawn hill site; a second Seowon city is worth more than anything else the capital can build.
Placed on the pinned second-ring hill the turn Writing lands; half the cost of a Campus, and the State Workforce Inspiration when it finishes.
A Mine on a ring hill and a Farm on a ring flat for Craftsmanship; the Mine gains its Science the turn the Seowon completes.
City three on the next drawn hill; Seowon cities, not wonders, are the ceiling.
Culture for Political Philosophy and Recorded History; Korea's civics lag its techs all game.
Only if a barbarian camp can see the capital; otherwise skip it and start the third Settler.

research.note: First. Every ring hill becomes a Mine, and nothing else in the opening needs a tech.
Second, because Writing requires it; no Eureka exists, so research it straight.
Third, for the Seowon; the Eureka comes from the Scout's first contact.

civics.note: Chiefdom's two slots: Discipline and God King.
Inspiration from three ring tiles improved; Ilkum for the Builders every ring needs.

policies.why: Faith toward the pantheon; this plan builds no Holy Site and needs 25 Faith from somewhere.
The Slinger and Warrior hold the capital against the first barbarians.
Replaces God King once the pantheon is founded; three ring tiles per city need Builders.

districts.note: Second ring, on the pinned hill, with nothing ever beside it; +4 Science from the turn it finishes.

pantheon.why: +1 Great Scientist point from every Seowon with a Library, and the plan builds one in every city.

city_states.why: The first envoy is Science in the capital; the Scout finds them on the way to the rival.

checkpoints.test: Capital on or beside a hill, the Seowon hill pinned in the second ring with three or more free ring tiles, Mining in, and the Scout past the first rival's border?
checkpoints.pass: Continue; draw the full settle map before the Settler finishes.
checkpoints.fail: No Seowon hill pinned: pin the best second-ring hill now, even with two free ring tiles. No contact yet: keep the Scout moving and accept a late Writing rather than a detour.

checkpoints.test: Writing in, the Seowon placed on its pin, the first Settler out toward city two's hill, and cities two to eight drawn with their hills, rings and far sides?
checkpoints.pass: Enter the execute phase and follow the map.
checkpoints.fail: Map not drawn: hold the Settler one turn and draw it. Seowon placed off its pin: it stays there for good, so redraw the ring and the far side around where it actually is.

tasks.text: Before moving the Settler, list the second- and third-ring hills and pick the Seowon hill with three or more free ring tiles.
Settle on or beside a hill, never on the Seowon hill, so that hill sits in the second ring.
Mark the Seowon hill, its six ring tiles, and the far side for the Commercial Hub, Theater Square, Industrial Zone and Aqueduct.
Scout toward the nearest rival, logging every cluster of hills and every city-state; Writing Eureka on first contact.
Place the Seowon on its pin the turn Writing completes and keep it in the queue until it finishes.
Draw cities two to eight with their Seowon hills, rings and far sides before the second Settler is queued.
Write the Governor plan down: Pingala in the capital takes every promotion; one more Governor; no third until Pingala has three promotions.

phases.name: Follow the map
phases.objective: Settle cities two to seven on their drawn sites, make each city's first district its Seowon on the pin, mine and farm and work every ring, establish Pingala in the capital and promote him, and slot Natural Philosophy by turn 70. Low decision density by design; the work is placing what turn 20 drew.

build_order.why: Cities four to seven on the drawn hills, with Colonization slotted.
First district in every new city, on its pin; chop the ring's Woods into it.
Mines on every ring hill and Farms on every ring flat before any other improvement.
In every Seowon; Divine Spark pays from it and Recorded History counts the districts.
Capital, far side, touching the center; the first Trade Route for Currency.
Capital, touching the Commercial Hub; the third district type for Mathematics and Culture to keep civics in step.
One in each border city facing a rival; Korea builds Science, not soldiers.

research.note: Archers for the border cities; the Slinger's kill gave the Eureka.
A Mine on a ring resource gives the Eureka.
Trade Route from the capital to city two.
Iron on a ring hill is a Mine that also earns Science.
Seowon, Commercial Hub and Theater Square give the Eureka.
Three ring Mines are long done; Production for every Seowon building.
Ancient Walls in the border city facing the nearest rival.

civics.note: Colonization for cities four to seven; six population is free.
Inspiration from the pantheon; the Inspiration card for Great Scientist points.
Classical Republic for Great Person points; three city-states met give the Inspiration.
Two Seowons give the Inspiration; Natural Philosophy doubles every Seowon.

policies.why: Settlers faster for the four remaining near sites.
One Production in every city while each builds its Seowon.
Doubles Campus adjacency, and the Seowon's flat +4 is its adjacency: +8 in every isolated Seowon.
Great Scientist points on top of Divine Spark and the Seowons.

districts.note: First district, on the drawn hill, nothing beside it.
Far side, touching the City Center; Gold and the first Trade Route.
Far side, touching the Commercial Hub, never the ring.

pantheon.why: Founded around turn 30 from God King; pays from the first Library.

wonders.name: Great Library
wonders.why: Science, two Great Work of Writing slots and the Ancient and Classical Eurekas still missing; it must sit on flat land beside a Seowon with a Library, and a wonder there costs the Seowon nothing.
wonders.skip_if: Recorded History lands after turn 65, an AI has already started it, or the only flat tile beside a Seowon is a ring Farm the city works.

governors.why: The first title: Science and Culture in the biggest city, and every later promotion on him adds Hwarang's three percent there.
The first Hwarang promotion; Science per citizen in the city that works the most ring Mines.
Half again as much from chopping the Woods off ring hills into Seowons and Settlers; Provision is his first promotion.

city_states.why: Science in every city while at peace with every civilization, which is Korea's normal state.
Faster growth in every Seowon city, and the ring Farms already feed them.
Three envoys in any Scientific city-state add Science to every Library.

great_people.why: The first one is the Education Eureka; Hypatia, if offered, adds Science to every Library and every Seowon has one.

checkpoints.test: Four cities each with a Seowon on its pin, four or more ring Mines worked, Pingala established in the capital, and the pantheon founded?
checkpoints.pass: Continue to cities five to seven.
checkpoints.fail: A city with no Seowon yet: chop its ring Woods into it before anything else. Pingala missing: the next title goes to him the turn it arrives.

checkpoints.test: Six or seven cities, every Seowon with a Library, Natural Philosophy slotted, and Science first on the scoreboard?
checkpoints.fail: Science second or lower: count Seowons that touch a district or sit in the first ring. More than one means the ceiling is already lower; settle the remaining drawn sites before any wonder.

tasks.text: Found Divine Spark, or Religious Settlements if it lands before turn 30 and a drawn site is still free.
First Governor title to Pingala in the capital; the second to Magnus in city two.
Four cities, four Seowons on their pins, ring Mines worked before any other tile.
Recorded History in and Natural Philosophy slotted the same turn.
A Library in every Seowon; the far-side districts placed in the capital, none touching a ring.

phases.name: Hold the lead
phases.objective: Universities in every Seowon, the Government Plaza on a far-side tile, Pingala at three or more promotions, and one decision at Machinery: whether a Hwacha war buys enough hills to be worth it. Steady, unspectacular Science lead.

build_order.why: Every Seowon; Printing at two, Astronomy in the city whose Seowon touches a Mountain.
On the far side of the capital or city two, never on a ring; the Ancestral Hall gives every later city a free Builder for its ring.
Two per border city facing a hostile neighbour, or four for the Hwacha window.
Capital, on a tile that does not touch the Seowon; Military Engineering and Housing.
Two, in the Commercial Hubs, for Guilds and the free Banking Eureka.

research.note: Universities; the first Great Scientist gave the Eureka.
The Hwacha; usually unboosted.
The capital Aqueduct, placed away from the Seowon.
Two Universities.
The University in the Seowon pinned beside a Mountain.
A Lumber Mill on Woods outside every ring.

civics.note: Six Farms, half of them in rings; Serfdom.
The capital at ten population on ring Farms.
A Research Alliance with the highest-Science neighbour.

policies.why: Still the best card in the game for this empire.
Builders with more charges for the rings of cities six to eight.
Great Scientist points while the Universities fill.

districts.note: Far side; its extra Governor title is a Hwarang promotion.
On a tile that touches the City Center and not the Seowon.

governors.why: Culture per citizen keeps civics close to the techs, and it is another Hwarang promotion.
Great Person points doubled in the capital; the Seowon there makes the most Great Scientist points.

city_states.why: A Great Person point from every district with a building; every Seowon has a Library.
Science for every improved strategic resource type, and Korea mines them all.

great_people.why: Medieval and Renaissance Great Scientists whose bonuses land on Libraries and Universities, which every Seowon holds.

checkpoints.test: Universities in three Seowons, Pingala on three promotions, and two Hwacha in each border city that faces a hostile neighbour?
checkpoints.pass: Continue; the rest of the Universities and the Government Plaza.
checkpoints.fail: Pingala short of promotions: a title went to a new Governor; give every next title to him. No Hwacha and a neighbour massing: buy two now, before the Universities.

checkpoints.test: Every Seowon with a University, the Government Plaza built, and Science first by at least a quarter over the next civilization?
checkpoints.fail: Under a quarter: settle or capture any remaining drawn hill site and work every ring Mine before building anything else.

tasks.text: At Machinery, run the Hwacha window trigger: one war for hills, or two Hwacha per border city and peace.
Government Plaza on a far-side tile; spend its title on a promotion.
Universities in four Seowons; Printing and Astronomy collected.
Research Alliance signed with the friendliest high-Science civilization.

phases.name: Live inside the ceiling
phases.objective: Rivals with high-adjacency Campuses start to close the gap here. The answer is Industrial Zones beside the ring Mines, Rationalism, Oxford University, Research Labs and any drawn site still empty, not new districts beside the Seowons. Communism at Class Struggle, and two flat Spaceport tiles reserved by turn 210.

build_order.why: Two, each placed to touch a ring's outer Mines but not the Seowon.
In both; Class Struggle at three.
Power for the Factories and the Research Labs.
Every Seowon as soon as Chemistry allows.

research.note: Free from Guilds.
Free from The Enlightenment; Oxford University.
Two Workshops in the Industrial Zones.
A Mine on Niter, ideally in a ring.
Research Labs; the Research Alliance at level 2 gives the Eureka.

civics.note: Three Great Scientists give the Inspiration; Rationalism.
Merchant Republic as the Tier 2 government; usually unboosted.
Three Factories; Communism and Five-Year Plan.

policies.why: Science from every Seowon building, with the extra for districts at +3 adjacency or more; every isolated Seowon qualifies.
Replaces Natural Philosophy and doubles Industrial Zone adjacency as well as the Seowon's.

districts.city: the two cities with the most ring Mines
districts.note: Touching the ring's outer Mines, not the Seowon; Ruhr Valley beside one if a river allows.

wonders.name: Oxford University
wonders.why: Two free technologies and Science in its city; it goes on flat Grassland or Plains beside a Seowon with a University.
wonders.skip_if: Scientific Theory lands after turn 185, or the only qualifying tile is a ring Farm the city works.

wonders.name: Ruhr Valley
wonders.why: Production in its city and on every Mine there; the ring Mines make it the Spaceport city.
wonders.skip_if: No river tile touches an Industrial Zone with a Factory, or Industrialization lands after turn 190.

governors.why: District Production for the Industrial Zone and later the Spaceport; his promotions count for Hwarang there too.

city_states.why: Production toward city projects, which is every space project the next phase runs.

great_people.why: Charges into Oxford University and Ruhr Valley.
Industrial Great Scientists for free techs and Research Lab Science.

checkpoints.test: Rationalism slotted, two Industrial Zones with Factories and a Coal Power Plant, Oxford built or skipped, and Chemistry in?
checkpoints.pass: Continue; Research Labs in every Seowon.
checkpoints.fail: Behind on Industrial Zones: build them in the two ring-Mine cities only, and skip any wonder still queued.

checkpoints.test: Communism adopted, Five-Year Plan slotted, Rocketry within ten turns, and a flat Spaceport tile reserved in the capital and the Ruhr city?
checkpoints.fail: No flat far-side tile left: use one that touches the Seowon only in the second city and accept the lost point; the capital's Spaceport takes priority.

tasks.text: Two Industrial Zones placed against ring Mines, neither touching a Seowon.
Rationalism slotted the turn The Enlightenment completes.
Reserve a flat tile on the far side of the capital and of the Ruhr city for Spaceports.

phases.name: Launch
phases.objective: Finish the space race before the ceiling matters: Spaceports in the capital and the Ruhr city, Pingala on Space Initiative, Hong Kong held, every Great Engineer into projects, Counterspies on both Spaceports, and the Exoplanet Expedition launched by about turn 250.

build_order.why: Capital and the Ruhr city, on the flat far-side tiles reserved at turn 205.
Counterspies in both Spaceport cities; one on Disrupt Rocketry if a rival's Spaceport is ahead.
Any Seowon still without one; the projects need their techs on time.

research.note: The Coal Power Plant already gave the Eureka.
Spaceports and the Earth Satellite; no Eureka exists.
Free from Communism.
An Oil Well for Power.
The Moon Landing; usually unboosted.
A Mine on Aluminum.

civics.note: Free from the first Research Lab.

policies.why: Seowon and Industrial Zone adjacency doubled to the end.
Research Lab Science in every Seowon to the end.

districts.note: Flat, far side, touching no Seowon.

governors.why: Production toward space projects in the capital Spaceport, and another Hwarang promotion.

great_people.why: Atomic and Information Great Engineers add Production to space projects; buy them with Gold if the points are short.
Free techs bring the next project forward.

checkpoints.test: Earth Satellite and Moon Landing done, the Mars Colony under way, and no rival with more space projects complete?
checkpoints.fail: A rival ahead: run the space race slips trigger, with Spies on its Spaceport and every Great Engineer on your projects.

checkpoints.test: Exoplanet Expedition launched and the laser station projects shortening its trip?
checkpoints.fail: Not launched: the game is a Score game unless your military tech is ahead of the leader's, in which case run the Domination secondary against its Spaceport city.

tasks.text: Spaceports started in the capital and the Ruhr city the turn Rocketry lands.
Counterspies on both Spaceport districts before the first project begins.
Exoplanet Expedition launched; every remaining Great Engineer into the laser stations.

The University in the Seowon pinned beside a Mountain at turn 0.
A Lumber Mill on Woods outside every ring.
An Armory only if an Encampment was built for the Hwacha war.
Guilds is on the civic path.
The Enlightenment is on the civic path.
Workshops in the two Industrial Zones beside the ring Mines.

Clearing a camp, which Korea does only when it can see the capital.

Researching Construction for the Water Mill.

The capital at fifteen population with its Aqueduct.

The first Spaceport.

decision_triggers.name: A site without its hill
decision_triggers.if: Fog cleared over a drawn site shows no hill in its second ring, or the hill's ring is mostly another city's tiles.
decision_triggers.then: Skip the site and settle the next drawn one. A Korean city with no Seowon hill has no Science district at all; it is a Settler spent on Housing and Amenity pressure.

decision_triggers.name: A district wants the ring
decision_triggers.if: The only legal tile for an Aqueduct, Dam, Neighborhood or Spaceport in a city touches its Seowon.
decision_triggers.then: Accept the permanent lost point only for an Aqueduct in a city that must pass ten population, or for a Spaceport in the second Spaceport city. Never for a Commercial Hub, Theater Square, Industrial Zone or Government Plaza; they always have another tile.

decision_triggers.name: The Hwacha window
decision_triggers.if: Machinery is in, and a neighbour has two or more cities with unused hills within eight tiles of your border, defended by Medieval units and without Medieval Walls.
decision_triggers.then: Build four Hwacha and two melee units in the nearest cities, take those two cities, pin a Seowon hill in each the turn it falls, and make peace. One war only; the Seowon count is the goal, not the map.

decision_triggers.name: Rival adjacency overtakes
decision_triggers.if: Between turns 150 and 200 a rival's Science per turn passes yours.
decision_triggers.then: Expected; it is the ceiling showing. Do not chase it with districts beside the Seowons. Fill the last drawn sites, finish Pingala's promotions, take Taruga and Hong Kong, and bring the Spaceport forward.

decision_triggers.name: The space race slips
decision_triggers.if: At turn 220 a rival has more space projects complete, or is a full era ahead in techs.
decision_triggers.then: Two Spies on Disrupt Rocketry against its Spaceport city, Counterspies on your own, and every Great Engineer into your projects. Turn to the Domination secondary only if your military techs match its; never start a war against a civilization that out-techs you.

abort.trigger: Turn 0 finds no hill within two moves that can host a second-ring Seowon, or turn 50 arrives with fewer than three cities that have a Seowon on its pin.
actions: Say plainly that Korea is now a generic civ with Hwarang, and stop founding cities without hills.
Build Seowons wherever a hill exists, even beside the City Center at +3, and put Pingala in the capital with every promotion.
Target a faster finish: take a hill-rich neighbour with Hwacha at Machinery for the Seowon sites the start lacked, then race for Spaceports with what you hold.

fail_state: Turn 120 with five cities, two of them on flat land with no Seowon, the others' Seowons in the first ring or squeezed between a Commercial Hub and an Aqueduct at +2, ring Mines left unworked, and every Governor title spent on a new Governor with no promotions. Science is third instead of first, and none of it can be fixed: districts do not move, promotions do not refund, and the hills were chosen by turn 20.
common_mistakes: Placing the Seowon in the first ring because the hill is closer. It touches the City Center and stays at +3 for the whole game.
Putting the Aqueduct, Government Plaza or a Neighborhood beside the Seowon because the tile was free. Every adjacent district costs a point of Science forever, two under Natural Philosophy.
Spreading Governor titles over five Governors. Hwarang pays per promotion; Pingala with five promotions in the capital is worth more than four Governors with none.
Leaving ring Mines unworked. The Three Kingdoms Science is a tile yield and only counts while a citizen works the tile.
Settling a good flat site with no hill. Korea has no Campus, so that city never has a Science district.
Playing a long game. The lead is widest around turn 150; every turn spent past turn 260 is a turn rivals' adjacency spends catching up.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset (Korea, Seondeok, Hwarang, Three Kingdoms, Seowon, Hwacha, Cheomseongdae).

Where the civ-info text differs from the game, the game is followed: the Seowon has a flat +4 Science that drops by 1 for each adjacent district, and the +1 Science and +1 Food of Three Kingdoms land on the adjacent Mines and Farms, not on the Seowon as adjacency. The Hwacha is unlocked by Machinery, a Medieval technology, not in the Renaissance era.

The caveat that sources cite both +3 and +4 is read as the same district in two placements: +4 isolated, +3 when it touches one district, most often the City Center from the first ring. The plan does not rely on any Mountain, Reef or natural wonder adjacency for the Seowon; the affinity notes on Yosemite and the Great Barrier Reef are read as tile yields for the ring.
